findings.quote: nothing in this set has a dollar sign on it. Every chart is about time or case counts

the same category carries different text depending on viewport, which would be confusing if someone tried to cite or cross-reference a category name between the two versions
two smooth, parallel, plausible-looking lines that never diverge or spike is visually reassuring, not alarming

rejected_reasons.no dollar figures: The source carries no cost data at all - no spend, no timekeeper, no rate. Recorded as a stated limit in docket-to-matter.md L-03. A chart cannot invent it, and the seat's point is the strongest argument for the module's own scope statement.
rejected_reasons.no owner or approval date on the chart: Ownership and as-of are page-level, in the disclosure block and the provenance strip. Repeating them on five canvases is not what 4.2 asks for.
rejected_reasons.category names differ between widths: A declared abbreviation mapping, which Rule 5.5 permits explicitly and prefers to deleting a label. The mapping is in the source and named in the review.
rejected_reasons.the calm parallel lines undercut the ala: That is the finding, not a defect. The chart exists to show that a broken method looks reassuring in this cut.
rejected_reasons.near-zero bars are hairlines: Drawn at true scale deliberately. Rescaling or dropping them would hide that five rules move the answer by less than a day between them, which is the honest reading.
rejected_reasons.counts not on chart 5: Percentages are on the bars because the title makes a percentage claim; counts are in the tooltip and the table. Rule 4.4 names the tooltip as the home for full precision.
